subject.title: Externally-registered cron jobs auto-enable without user confirmation, inherit expensive default model, no usage circuit breaker

question: What default security policy should OpenClaw apply before externally or plugin-registered recurring agentTurn cron jobs can run on an inherited model?
rationale: The source reproduction is clear, but the fix changes shipped cron defaults, plugin scheduling contracts, provider/model cost policy, quota thresholds, and upgrade behavior, so automation cannot safely choose the boundary.

options.title: Require explicit activation
options.body: Recurring externally or plugin-registered agentTurn jobs should be created disabled or approval-pending unless an operator explicitly enables them with visible model/cost information and a doctor/update migration path.

options.title: Warn only on inherited expensive models
options.body: Keep current activation semantics but warn or block only when a recurring agentTurn job inherits a high-cost default model without a job-specific model.

options.title: Split into narrower guardrails
options.body: Resolve the consent, reason-aware backoff, cost-budget, and scheduling-provenance pieces independently through the linked issues, accepting that this combined behavior remains unresolved for now.

recommendation.title: Require explicit activation
recommendation.body: Recurring externally or plugin-registered agentTurn jobs should be created disabled or approval-pending unless an operator explicitly enables them with visible model/cost information and a doctor/update migration path.

likelyOwner.reason: CODEOWNERS already routes security-sensitive cron paths to this team, and the open question is the operator-consent boundary for unattended scheduled model calls.
